title: Townsend Brown parachutes into Germany to probe German UFO program and Foo Fighters

tellings.quote: He parachuted behind enemy lines into Germany in 1944
and from a very low altitude parachuted behind enemy lines into Germany,
tellings.difference: Dated 1945 rather than 1944, says he jumped from very low altitude, and credits O'Reilly.
tellings.link_reason: This is the same story of Brown parachuting behind enemy lines into Germany, credited to Schatzkin's account.

as_told.title: Brown parachuted behind enemy lines in Germany

tellings.quote: The TICOM mission, which Brown was associated with, took place in East Germany. Brown was captured by the Nazis and made a prisoner of war just to get rescued shortly thereafter by the Americans.

tellings.link_reason: This is the same wartime mission into Germany that Brown took part in, as in telling 8 and the parachute story.

as_told.title: TICOM mission and Brown captured as POW

plain: The American inventor Townsend Brown, later described as a CIA scientist, is said to have parachuted behind enemy lines into Germany near the end of World War II to look into a German program on flying craft and the Foo Fighters, the glowing balls of light Allied pilots reported. Michels tells it in 1944, crediting Brown's biographer Paul Schatzkin and his book The Man Who Mastered Gravity, while Schatzkin himself tells Michels the jump came in 1945, from very low altitude, crediting a man named O'Reilly. In another episode Michels adds that Brown was tied to an Allied mission he names TICOM in East Germany, was captured by the Nazis and held as a prisoner of war, and was rescued by the Americans soon after.
